summary: Pipeline output is well-structured and paper-faithful. All Pass 0 structured invariants pass: gradient-embedding computation, k-MEANS++ seeding, and retrain-from-scratch protocol are correctly implemented. The required forward_with_embedding model hook is present with correct semantics. One important finding: the notebook imports scikit-learn for PCA visualization but it is missing from requirements.txt. Two minor cosmetic inconsistencies in notebook TOC numbering and data format documentation.

findings.description: The notebook imports scikit-learn (`from sklearn.decomposition import PCA`) for the 2D gradient embedding projection plot, but scikit-learn is not listed in requirements.txt. A researcher who follows the Quick Start (`pip install -r requirements.txt`) and then runs the notebook will get an ImportError at this cell.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `scikit-learn` to requirements.txt. Alternatively, replace the PCA visualization with a pure numpy matplotlib scatter plot using two embedding dimensions directly.

findings.description: The table of contents lists §5 ('Running active learning end-to-end') and then jumps to §5.2 ('Learning curve'), skipping §5.1 ('The acquisition loop'). The field guide declares a 5.1 subsection for the acquisition loop, and the corresponding code cell exists, but lacks the ### 5.1 markdown heading anchor.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `### 5.1 The acquisition loop` markdown subsection heading before the acquisition loop code cell, or add the 5.1 entry to the table of contents.

findings.location: cell 20 (§6 Use your own data, CSV format table)
findings.description: The §6 markdown describes CSV format as having a '`y` column' but data.py's implementation reads the last column as the label regardless of column name. The description should say 'last column is the label' to match the implementation.
findings.proposed_fix: Update the CSV format description in §6 to match data.py's actual behavior: 'last column is the integer label, all other columns are float features'.
